summary: Preserve standard Windows runtime inputs in bounded consumer checks.

details.problem: The bounded Windows child environment omitted standard runtime inputs used by supported consumer bootstrap checks, so a managed processctl command could fail while the same command passed in the ambient runner.
details.changes: The managed projection now retains OS, ProgramFiles, and ProgramFiles(x86) alongside LOCALAPPDATA, while continuing to exclude unrelated ambient values, Python path injection, and secret-marked inputs.
details.apply: Adopt engineering-process v3.2.3 through the consumer's existing hash-locked process runner, regenerate managed files, and rerun the consumer's Windows processctl profile.
details.compatibility: Non-breaking additive patch release. Existing v3.2.2 locks remain valid; consumers must adopt v3.2.3 to receive the corrected Windows projection, while arbitrary ambient environment state remains excluded.
details.notes: The release does not change consumer-owned commands or product behavior. The originating LyricRail issue is closed only after a real post-adoption managed Windows profile passes.
